title: City Council District 1
statement: Brooklyn's sentiment sits just under the city line and its trajectory is still decay — but the retail number moved up and the crime index is flat to city. What I take from that is not a crisis and not a victory; it is a neighborhood that needs its record kept honestly. West Oakland, my other turf, is a different story: sentiment 0.41, crime down, and a housing pressure reading that ticked up a full point. I am not going to invent a problem where the numbers do not show one, and I am not going to pretend the pressure line is nothing. This week I put a work move into the Youth Apprenticeship Pipeline, stalled on my board, because Brooklyn and West Oakland young people signed up and I still owe them a placement path, not a sign-up sheet. And I will say plainly that the one complaint in my window — the Stabilization Fund complaint naming two households out of a program's record — is a thing I will answer with the record, not with a speech. The Tenant Defense Fund I sponsored is operational; I am not relitigating it. No new spending program this week without a need I can name from the pack.
